{{verse|chapter=11|verse=16}} And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 7, 31.''}}* vvherevnto {{ls}}hal I e{{ls}}teeme this generation to be like? It is like to children {{ls}}itting in the market-place: {{verse|chapter=11|verse=17}} vvhich crying to their companions, {{ls}}ay, We haue piped to you, and you haue not daunced: we haue lamented, and you haue not mourned. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=18}} For {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 3, 4.''}}* Iohn came neither eating nor drinking: and they {{ls}}ay, He hath a diuel. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=19}} The Sonne of man came {{sup|‖}} eating and drinking, and they {{ls}}ay, Behold a man that is a glotton and a vvinedrinker, a frende of Publicans and {{ls}}inners. And vvi{{ls}}edom is iu{{ls}}tified of her children.

{{verse|chapter=11|verse=20}} Then {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 10, 13.''}}* began he to vpbraide the cities, vvherein vvere done the mo{{ls}}t of his miracles, for that they had not done penance. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=21}} Wo be to thee Corozain, vvo be to thee Beth-{{ls}}aida: for if in Tyre & Sidon had been vvrought the miracles that haue been vvrought in you, they had done {{sup|‖}} penance in hearecloth and a{{ls}}hes long agoe. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=22}} But neuerthele{{ls}}{{ls}}e, I {{ls}}ay to you, it {{ls}}hal be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the day of iudgement, then for you. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=23}} And thou Capharnaum, {{ls}}halt thou be exalted vp to heauen? thou {{ls}}halt come dovvne euen vnto hel. for if in Sodom had been vvrought the miracles that haue been wrought in thee, perhaps it had remained vnto this day. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=24}} But notvvith{{ls}}tanding I {{ls}}ay to you, that it {{ls}}hal be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of iudgement, then for thee.

And no man knovveth the Sonne but the Father: neither doth any knovv the Father, but the Sonne, and to vvhom it {{ls}}hal plea{{ls}}e the Sonne to reueale. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=28}} Come ye to me al that labour, and are burdened, and I vvil refre{{ls}}h you. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=29}} Take vp my yoke vpon you, and learne of me, becau{{ls}}e I am meeke, and humble of hart: and you {{ls}}hal finde re{{ls}}t to your {{ls}}oules. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=30}} For my {{sup|‖}} yoke is {{ls}}vveete, and my burden light.⊣<noinclude>{{rh||D iij|Annot-}}</noinclude>
